context: David's psalm of the Lord as a shepherd who leads, restores and stays near, even in the darkest valley.
Jesus invites the tired and burdened to come to him and find rest.
God's promise to Israel in exile: do not be afraid, I am with you and will hold you up.
God's charge to Joshua as he takes over from Moses and leads the people into a new land.
Paul, writing from prison, tells a church he loves to bring every worry to God in prayer.
Jesus comforts his friends the night before he dies, and leaves them his peace.
Paul's blessing near the end of his letter to the church in Rome.
From Jeremiah's letter to exiles in Babylon: settle in, seek the good of the city, and trust that God has a future for you.
In the middle of a book of grief over a ruined city, the writer remembers that God's mercies are new every morning.
Comfort for a weary people: those who wait for the Lord will renew their strength.
A song of trust in God when the world seems to be falling apart.
Paul on a weakness he asked God to take away, and the answer he was given.
Short, practical encouragements at the end of Paul's earliest letter.
A festival song of thanks: this is the day the Lord has made.
The opening of a long psalm of thanks from people God rescued in many ways.
Paul's description of love, written to a church divided by rivalry.
A proverb on the friend who loves at all times.
Two are better than one: if one falls, the other can help them up.
Jesus to his disciples, whom he calls friends, on the greatest love.
How to live together: kind, tender-hearted, forgiving one another.
Bearing with one another and forgiving, as the Lord forgave you.
If you lack wisdom, ask God, who gives generously.
A father's advice to trust the Lord rather than your own understanding.
Paul on how God works for good in all things for those who love him.
The Lord is near to the broken-hearted.
From the Beatitudes at the start of the Sermon on the Mount: blessed are those who mourn.
The vision of a new heaven and earth, where every tear is wiped away.
If anyone is in Christ, they are a new creation.
Do not dwell on the past: God is doing a new thing.
Don't grow tired of doing good; in due season you will reap.
Part of Paul's list of what love looks like in practice.
What does the Lord require: to act justly, love mercy and walk humbly.
An evening psalm: I will lie down and sleep in peace.
The priestly blessing Aaron and his sons were to speak over the people.
Paul, writing from prison, tells his friends in Philippi that every memory of them makes him thankful.
Paul asks a young church to keep encouraging one another and building each other up.
Carry each other's loads; that is how the law of Christ is lived out.
Part of Paul's picture of real love in a community: warm affection, and honouring one another.
At the last supper Jesus gives a new commandment: love one another as I have loved you.
John writes that love comes from God, so everyone who loves has been born of God.
The elder John opens a letter to his dear friend Gaius with a prayer for his health and wellbeing.
A proverb comparing a friend's heartfelt counsel to perfume and oil that delight the heart.
Keep thinking of ways to stir one another to love and good works, and keep meeting together.
